text:
Matt: quick check — before we update the RFC, want to align on 'soft fallback' semantics across region/tier/variant adapters. proposing a small adapter contract so adapters can signal 'soft' fallback reason instead of nil.

Sara: +1. today adapters return Optional/Route and nil is treated as hard fallback; we lose the 'acceptable-but-not-preferred' signal.

Jin: what's the shape? concerned about perf if we carry metadata.

Matt: sketch: policy.evaluate(...) -> { status: accept | soft_fallback | hard_fallback, candidate?: Route, reason_id?: string, priority_delta?: int }

Ben: so runtime sees soft_fallback and can still try the route but annotate tokens/traces? :thinking_face: \ .

Matt: yes. soft_fallback == 'we don't prefer it but it's acceptable under certain SLAs or cost policies'. runtime can pick cheaper/closer route and tag telemetry with reason_id.

Carla: avoid explosion of freeform strings. prefer enums: capacity_limited, latency_degraded, model_quantized_quality_drop.

Sara: enum + optional freeform for debug only. telemetry records enum; freeform stored in debug logs (sampled).

Jin: perf: status as a byte, candidate pointer unchanged, reason id as small int, priority_delta small int — negligible overhead.

Ben: compatibility with many v1 adapters expecting Optional/Route? migration path?

Matt: runtime will talk to both v1 and v2. v1 adapters => implicit hard_fallback. add a compatibility shim mapping nil -> hard_fallback. v2 can emit soft_fallback and enums.

Carla: tests: ordering when soft_fallbacks present; canary traffic to verify soft->accept transitions and no thrash.

Sara: ops: add telemetry metric soft_fallback_rate per tenant/model/region. alert if > 5% for 5m on prod-only tiers.

opssentry-bot: deploy-log: canary/sandbox policy-engine:v2 deployed 2024-05-01T09:12:03Z :rocket:

Jin: rollout plan: v2 to Dedicated first (predictable capacity), then hosted API. run a 24h sim against recent traces to detect policy thrash.

Matt: next steps: Sara prototype v2 adapter shape + shim tests (due Thu); Jin add telemetry fields + sim harness (due Fri); Carla enumerate normalized enums and map existing reasons (due Thu); Ben update policy docs + migration notes (pair on examples) (due Mon).

Sara: assigned. I'll open PR for adapter types and a short spec.

Ben: I'll draft docs pages and a migration checklist.

Carla: I'll post mapping doc to #architecture by EOD.

Matt: one open question: how should runtime routing priority treat SoftFallback when tenant sets strict latency SLA? should policy->runtime expose a priority_delta so SLAs can override?

Jin: propose optional priority_delta:int (negative -> prefer more, positive -> deprioritize). default 0 for accept, maybe +10 for soft_fallback. runtime honors SLA override.

Sara: keep priority_delta optional; runtime should only consider it when tenant SLA != strict. otherwise SLA wins.

Matt: ok consensus: include optional priority_delta and enum reason_id. runtime will respect SLA override. we'll add this to the RFC.

opssentry-bot: note: created ticket INF-1427 'policy-engine adapter v2 + soft_fallback rollout' assigned to @Sara, @Jin, @Carla, @Ben.

Matt: thanks all. Sara — ping when PR is ready and I'll merge RFC update. :thumbsup:

Sara: will do. thanks!
